we propose a novel framework that allows for the resource allocation in a network with multiple static priority schedulers, in the presence of statistical QoS requirements, for traffic flows with bounded variance.

, in this paper, we propose a general framework for the resource allocation, the admission control, and the performance evaluation of networks of static priority service disciplines, which can be applied to a wide class of sources with linear variance envelope, and we provide analytical closed-form solutions for the minimum link capacity and the maximum number of accepted flows, for all priority levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in a Static Priority scheduler, it is possible to provide differentiated statistical QoS targets in terms of delay and delay violation probability, for each traffic flow, by allocating the minimum capacity to the scheduler.

, for the first time, we provide a complete framework for resource allocation, admission control and performance evaluation of networks of static priority service disciplines, with statistical QoS constraints, which is based on the analysis of the isolated node and on the use of the network calculus.

the proposed framework allows the design and analysis of the resource allocation and the admission control of statistical QoS guarantees in networks of static priorities schedulers, by providing closed-form expressions for the minimum link capacity and for the maximum number of accepted traffic flows in each priority level, with statistical end-to-end QoS guarantees.
